elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Assess severity of episode:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Any of: pulse < 50, unable to talk, silent chest (tight chest but no wheeze), PEFR2 <33% of predicted, drowsy or confused?

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: No

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Yes: Life threatening

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Any of: oxygen saturation < 90%, respiratory rate > 30, pulse > 120, unable to talk in full sentences, PEFR2 <60% of predicted, agitated?

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Give 40% face mask oxygen (if known COPD, give 24-28% face mask oxygen), keep saturation 93-95% while preparing nebuliser and between nebulisations.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: No: Mild or moderate

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Yes: Severe

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Give inhaled salbutamol via spacer 400-1000mcg if required, or nebulise 1mL salbutamol 0.5% solution in 3mL sodium chloride 0.9%, with oxygen at flow rate of 8L/minute.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Refer urgently. While awaiting transport:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: If known asthma or COPD, give prednisone 40mg orally.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Nebulise 2mL (10mg) salbutamol 0.5% solution and 2mL (0.5mg) ipratropium bromide solution with oxygen at flow rate of 8L/minute.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Monitor response regularly. If no better, repeat salbutamol every 20 minutes during first hour.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Assess after 1 hour of treatment:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Check respiratory rate and PEFR2. Can patient talk normally?

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Give single dose hydrocortisone 100mg IM/slow IV.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Improving or no change:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Worsening despite treatment: Unable to talk normally or

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: If no better, repeat nebulisations every 20 minutes as needed for up to 4 doses in 2 hours. If no longer life threatening, manage as severe:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Able to talk normally and respiratory rate < 20 or

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: PEFR2 improved by > 20%

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: respiratory rate ≥ 20 or PEFR2 not improved

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Wheeze/tight chest resolved

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Wheeze/tight chest still present

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Give 40% face mask oxygen (if known COPD, give 24-28% face mask oxygen), keep saturation 93-95% while preparing nebuliser and between nebulisations.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Repeat salbutamol every 2-4 hours as needed.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Refer urgently. While awaiting transport:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Is wheeze/tight chest still present after 3 hours of treatment?

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Nebulise 1mL salbutamol 0.5% solution in 3mL sodium chloride 0.9% with oxygen at flow rate of 8L/minute, every 20 minutes or give instead inhaled salbutamol via spacer 400-1000mcg (4-10 puffs), every 20 minutes. If using spacer, deliver 1 puff at a time, allow patient to take 6 breaths through the spacer before next puff.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: If not already given, give single dose prednisone 40mg orally. If unable to take oral medication, give single dose hydrocortisone 100mg IM/slow IV.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: No

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Yes

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Assess response

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Discuss before discharge if any of: presents late afternoon, previous severe attacks, recent night time/ worsening of symptoms.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: Continue

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: If poor response, add 2mL (0.5mg) ipratropium bromide solution to 1mL salbutamol 0.5% solution and 1mL sodium chloride 0.9%, and nebulise every 20 minutes up to 3 doses only. If nebuliser unavailable, continue salbutamol 400-1000mcg (4-10 puffs) via spacer and add inhaled ipratropium bromide via spacer 80-160 mcg (2-4 puffs), every 20 minutes as needed for up to 3 hours.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: salbutamol every 2-4 hours as needed and refer.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: If first episode of wheeze/tight chest, assess for asthma and COPD 138.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: If still no better, repeat salbutamol nebulisations every 20 minutes until PEFR2 > 60% of predicted. Once PEFR2 > 60% of predicted, repeat every 2–4 hours as needed until referal.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with wheeze/tight chest:
elements.text: If known asthma/COPD, give routine care: if asthma 140, if COPD 141.

• If sudden wheeze/tight chest and any of: generalised itch/rash, face/tongue swelling, BP < 90/60, dizziness/collapse, abdominal pain, vomiting or exposure to possible allergen1, check for anaphylaxis 28. • If difficulty breathing worse on lying flat and leg swelling or patient ≥ 50 years with first episode of wheeze/tight chest, heart failure likely 151.
WHEEZE/TIGHT CHEST

1Common allergens include medication, food or insect bite/sting within the past few hours. 2Peak expiratory flow rate: PEFR is expressed as a percentage of the predicted normal value for the patients age and height 139.
